main_result: For full-column M and arbitrary N, let g=s_m(M) and c_1>=...>=c_m be the canonical correlations between Ran(M) and Ran(N). Then for every q=0,...,m-1, s_(m-q)(M+N)>=g sqrt(1-c_(q+1)^2). This is sharp even when N=GP for a symmetric signed added matrix. Thus q fully resonant/cancelled directions can be spent without any magnitude or rank bound on the remaining added packet.
qform_stability: For an ORIGINAL-coordinate carrier H, symmetric A_*, arbitrary symmetric G, additional rank-r carrier packet R0, and symmetric dense tail T with epsilon=||TP_H||, sqrt(lambda_(m-q-r)((A^2)[H,H])) >= [g sqrt(1-c_(q+1)^2)-epsilon]_+, where c_i compare Ran(A_*P_H) and Ran(GP_H). No random remainder is treated as independent noise.
density_corollary: If m-q-r>=5 and h=g sqrt(1-c_(q+1)^2)-epsilon>0, the completed five-square-mode compiler gives a continuous C0 density with ||p_Q||infinity<=sqrt(24*pi*m+K3^2)/h, K3=3*2^(4/3)*e^(1/3).
overlap_energy: With Omega=tr(Pi_R Pi_S)=sum c_i^2, c_(q+1)^2<=Omega/(q+1), hence s_(m-q)(M+N)>=g sqrt((1-Omega/(q+1))_+). Failure of a five-mode angle-spectrum exit forces high-dimensional near-alignment, not merely one bad direction.
